agyos_skill.intent: Use when starting a new implementation task and an issue must be created with strict acceptance criteria gating before execution.
agyos_skill.instructions: Create GitHub issues as the single tracking entrypoint for tasks, with a hard gate on acceptance criteria. Core rule: **no explicit, testable acceptance criteria from user => issue stays `draft` and execution is blocked.** - You are starting a new implementation task and want a GitHub issue to be the required tracking entrypoint. - The work must be blocked until the user provides explicit, testable acceptance criteria. - You need to distinguish between `draft`, `ready`, and `blocked` work before execution begins. Every issue must include these sections: - Problem - Goal - Scope - Non-Goals - Acceptance Criteria - Dependencies/Blockers - Status (`draft` | `ready` | `blocked` | `done`) Acceptance criteria are valid only when they are testable and pass/fail checkable. Examples: - valid: "CreateCheckoutLambda-dev returns an openable third-party payment checkout URL" - invalid: "fix checkout" / "improve UX" / "make it better" If criteria are missing or non-testable: - still create the issue - set `Status: draft` - add `Execution Gate: blocked (missing valid acceptance criteria)` - do not move task to execution Default mode is direct GitHub creation using `gh issue create`.
